Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

PART IV NETBALLS 

( Third Revision ) 



REAFFIRMED 



1. Scope — Covers dimensional and other requirements for netbalis excluding the bladders. 

2. Shape and Dimensions 

2.1 When fully inflated the ball shall be spherical in shape with circumference of 68 to 71 cm and 
the other characteristics shall be as specified in Fig. 1.

IS: 417 (Part IV)- 1976 

2.2 Mass of the ball with fully inflated bladder shall be 397 to 454 g. 

2.3 Colour — The colour of the balls shall be subject to requirements of the purchaser. 

3. Materials for Construction 

3.1 leader — The balls shall be manufactured from butt or bend portion of tight-textured cowhide, 
free from flay cuts and grain defects, vegetable or chrome tanned, dyed in any colour or pigmented 
as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. But at the end of tanning operation and 
before drying, suitable fungicides shall be incorporated into the leather for promoting resistance to 
mould growth in the leather; these shall be effective and non-toxic. The tanned leather shall be 
substantially fat-liquored or oiled or both and the surface obtained shall be smooth and well set. 

3.2 Thread for Stitching 

3.2.1 Linen thread — Rot-proofed and having 5 plies shall be used for stitching. The minimum 
breaking strength of single yarn shall be 4*5 kgf (45N) when tested as given in IS : 1670-1970 
•.Method for determination of breaking load, elongation at break and tenacity of yarns (first 
revision ) \ 

3.2.2 Cotton thread— Shall conform to variety No. 35 of IS: 1720-1969 'Specification for cotton 
sewing thread ( first revision ) ' and shall be rot-proofed. 

3.3 Lining Cloth— Subject to agreement between the purchaser and the supplier, netball covers 
may be provided with new cotton dritt or canvas lining. 

4. Construction and Workmanship 

4.1 The balls shall be made from a suitable number of panels of shapes capable of giving sphericity. 

4.2 Stitching — The balls shall be stitched with linen or cotton threads and shall have 24 to 25 
stitches per decimetre. The stitches shall be well-stretched. When the ball Is inflated fully the 
threads that are visible shall be not more than 2 mm deep from the surface of the ball. 

4.3 Mouth — The ball shall have its mouth as shown In Fig. 1. The mouth shall be adequate and 
shall permit the nozzle of the inflating pump or needle to be accommodated and suitable means 
provided to deflate the ball. The neck of the bladder shall be completely inside the mouth. 

5. Sampling and Inspection 

5.1 Sampling 

5.1.1 Lot — In any consignment, all the balls of one type manufactured from the same raw 
materials shall be grouped together to constitute a lot. 

5.1.2 Samples for test shall be selected at random from each lot in accordance with col 1 and 2 of 
Table 1. 

5.2 Inspection 

5.2.1 Each ball in the test samples shall first be examined for materials of construction as given 
under 3. If any ball in the test sample is noticed to have been made up of materials other than 
those specified, all the balls in the lot shall be examined and those not conforming shall be rejected. 

5.2.2 If the balls are made up of satisfactory materials, then each ball in the test sample shall be 
inspected for shape and dimensions (see 2), colour (see 2.3), construction and workmanship 
( see 4 ). 

5.2.3 During inspection of sample balls as in 5.2.2 each, instance of lack of conformity of the ball 
to the specification shall be considered as a defect of the ball. While examining sample balls, the 
total number and types of such defects shall be noted down. 

5.3 Criterion for Acceptance 

5.3.1 A lot shall be accepted as conforming to this standard, If the corresponding test samples 
satisfy the condition of 5.3.1.1 and 5.3.1.2. 

5.3.1.1 Total number of defects observed during testing as In 5.2.3 shall not be more than the 
corresponding acceptance number given in col 3 of Table 1. 



AMENDMENT NO. 1 JUNE 1978 
TO 
IS : 417 ( Part IV )-1976 SPECIFICATION FOR FOOTBALLS, VOLLEYBALLS 
BASKETBALLS, NETBALLS, THROWBALLS AND WATER-POLO BALLS ' 

PART IV NETBALLS 

( Third Revision ) 

Alterations 

(Page 1, clause 2.1, % lines 1 and 2 )— Delete the words 'and the Other characteristics shall be as 
specified in Fig. 1 \ 

( Page 1, Fig. 1 ) — Delete. 

^ Page, 2. clause 3.1 ) — Substitute the following foi the existing clause: 

4 3.1 Leather — The balls shall be manufactured from butt portion of tight-textured cowhide or 
buffalohide, free from flay cuts and grain defects, vegetable/semi-chrome or chrome tanned, dyed 
in any colour or pigmented as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. At the end of 
tanning operation, and before drying, suitable fungicides shall be incorporated into the leather for 
promonng resistance to mould growth in the leather, these shall be effective and non-toxic. The 
tanned leather shall be substantially fat-liquored or oiled or both and the surface obtained shall be 
smooth and well set. 

(Page 2. clause 3.2.2 ) - Substitute the following for the existing clause: 

"3.2.2 Cotton thread— Conforming to variety No. 35 [98 lex / 8 (6 s /8)] of IS: 1720-1969 
4 Specification for cotton sewing threads ( first revision ) '. " 

(Page 2, clause 4.2 ) — Substitute the following for the existing clause: 

4 4.2 Stitching — The ball shall be stitched with linen or cotton threads and shall have 24 — 2 
stitches per decimetre. The stitches shall be well stretched. When the ball is fully inflated, the 
visible threads shall be not more than 2 mm deep from the surface of the ball. The panels for 
netballs should preferably be cut with self-cutting-cum-perforating dies. 1 

( Page 2, clause 4.3, first sentence ) — Delete. 

Addendum 

( Page 1, clause 2.1 ) — Add the following new clause after 2.1: 
'2.1.1 A tolerance of 1 percent in the circumference on sphericity shall be allowed.'

•6. Marking — Unless otherwise required by the purchaser, each ball shall bear the manufacturer's 
name, Initials or trade-mark. 

4.1 ISI Certification Marking — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

7. Packing — Each ball shall first be wrapped In polyethylene cover and then packed together with 
other balls similarly wrapped according to the inetructions of the purchaser.
